text.tspan: On this machine: SHA-256 is 1.17× to 2.17× faster than BLAKE3; BLAKE3 is 1.54× to 3.79× faster than SHA-1DC
BLAKE3 SME2 matches BLAKE3 below 1 KiB and is up to 2.55× faster from there

svg.text: Line and dot: median · shaded band: minimum–maximum across 240 interleaved samples · single-threaded · lower is better
Hover a dot to compare contenders at that size · click a name at right to hide or show that contender

g.text: BLAKE3: blake3 1.8.7 · single-threaded; Rayon not enabled · platform NEON

g.text: SHA-256: sha2 0.10.9 (+sha2-asm 0.6.4) · assembly backends where available (ARMv8 SHA-256 instructions on AArch64)

g.text: SHA-1DC: sha1-checked 0.10.0 · SHA-1 with collision detection, pure Rust (the construction git uses)

g.text: BLAKE3 SME2: source https://github.com/johnservil/BLAKE3 · branch sme2-bench · commit 4ca9952c8522
BLAKE3 SME2: single-threaded; SME2 kernel for groups of sixteen chunks, integer + NEON hybrid kernels below that; the benchmark stops on a CPU without SME2
BLAKE3 at 64 B: one chunk → portable compression
